'''Kemba Hudley Walker''' (born May 8, 1990)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/kemba-walker|title=Kemba Walker|accessdate=2009-06-21}}</ref> is an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player. He is a {{convert|5|ft|11.75|in|m|2|abbr=on}} [[point guard]] for the [[University of Connecticut]].<ref>{{cite web|url =http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=41515|title=Kemba Walker profile on espn.go.com|accessdate=2011-03-15}}</ref>

==High school==
Walker grew up in the [[Soundview, Bronx|Soundview]] section of the Bronx. After a brief stint in [[Herbert H. Lehman High School]], he attended [[Rice High School (New York)|Rice High School]]. While there he was coached by Maurice Hicks, who coached other stand-outs like [[Andre Barrett]], [[Keydren Clark]], and [[Russell Robinson]]. In his junior year, Walker played against [[Simeon Career Academy]] and senior guard [[Derrick Rose]] in [[Madison Square Garden]] in a 53–51 win.<ref>{{cite news |publisher=USA Today
|url=http://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2007-01-11-rose-new-york_x.htm?POE=SPOISVA|title=Chicago standout Rose takes stage in New York|author=Lawlor, Christopher |date=January 11, 2007 |accessdate=January 30, 2011}}</ref> During Walker's senior year he averaged 18.2 points per game and 5.3 assists per game,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/EqSVKSBT_EGXkzbOjv4oFA/basketball-winter-07-08/stats-kemba-walker.htm|title=Kemba Walker Rice Basketball Stats 07-08|publisher=MaxPreps|accessdate=2009-06-21}}</ref> earning him a spot on the prestigious [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American Team]]. Kemba played for the New York Gauchos AAU basketball program with fellow [[Big East]] players Jordan Theodore, Darryl "Truck" Bryant, Devin Hill, and Danny Jennings.  The team went on to finish #1 in the nation.  Following high school he agreed to play for the University of Connecticut.

==College==
During his freshman year at UConn, Walker played in every game. He helped the Huskies achieve a number one seed in the [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2009 NCAA Tournament]]. Despite starting in only two games he averaged 25.5 minutes per game, far more than any regular non-starter.<ref>[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/teams/stats?teamId=41 Espn.com uconn huskies' team stats]</ref> He also helped the Huskies go to the 2009 [[Final Four]] with a 23 point effort in the [[Elite Eight]] vs [[Missouri University|Missouri]]. Walker appeared on one of the six regional covers ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''. Twelve games into his junior campaign, Walker was the nation's leading scorer, averaging 26.7 points per game. In addition, he averaged five rebounds and 3.8 assists per game.

In the [[2011 Big East Men's Basketball Tournament|2011 Big East Tournament]] (during his junior year), Walker hit the game winning shot as time expired to beat #3 overall [[2010–11 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]] and advance UConn to the semi-finals. He led UConn to victory over [[2010–11 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|University of Louisville]] in the Big East Championship game and was named MVP for the tournament. Walker scored 130 points in five games, a Big East Tournament record and the most points scored in any conference tournament in the past 15 seasons. UConn became the first school to win five games in five days to earn a conference championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310710097 |title=Connecticut Huskies vs. Louisville Cardinals - Recap |publisher=ESPN |date=2011-03-12 |accessdate=2011-03-22}}</ref>

On March 14, 2011, The United States Basketball Writers Association named Walker a first team All-American.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theday.com/article/20110314/INTERACT010103/110319839 |title=Walker named All-American |publisher=The Day |date=2011-03-14 |accessdate=2011-03-22}}</ref> He was picked to the Second Team All-America by [[Fox Sports]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Goodman|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711|title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams|work=[[Fox Sports]]||publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media|date=Mar 7, 2011|accessdate=June 21, 2011}}</ref> He was also a finalist for [[Oscar Robertson Trophy|College Basketball Player of the Year]] honors due to his performance in the 2010-11 season. Although he finished second, two journalists thought that Walker was the best player in college basketball that year.<ref>[http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/Jeff-Goodman-Brilliant-Kemba-Walker-paces-Connecticuts-run-to-Big-East-title-031211 Hard to argue Walker's POY candidacy, Jeff Goodman, FOXSports.com]</ref><ref>[http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/2011/03/12/2011-03-12_bronx_product_kemba_walker_has_dazzled_fans_with_clutch_play_at_uconn.html Bronx product Kemba Walker has dazzled fans with clutch play at UConn, Kevin Armstrong, NY Daily News]</ref>  Walker was named the winner of the [[Bob Cousy Award]] for the top point guard in the nation.<ref>[http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2011-03-30/report-kemba-walker-wins-bob-cousy-award Report: Kemba Walker wins Bob Cousy Award], accessed March 31, 2011</ref> On April 4, 2011 Walker led the University of Connecticut with 16 points in winning the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship]], and was named the [[NCAA Basketball Tournament Most Outstanding Player]].<ref>[http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/The-Unlikelys-Butler-and-UConn-play-for-it-all-01220612 UConn defeats Butler 53-41 for 3rd national title, Fox Sports, Associated Press]</ref> Walker was added to the [[Huskies of Honor]] upon the team's return from Houston at a pep rally to celebrate the National Title. He became the first men's basketball player to receive the honor since inaugural class was announced in December 2006.<ref>[http://www.mysanantonio.com/default/article/UConn-Men-Celebrate-With-Thousands-of-Fans-Kemba-1324249.php UConn Men Celebrate With Thousands of Fans; Kemba Walker's Jersey Retired. ''Journal Register News Service'', April 5, 2011]</ref>

==Professional career==
Walker announced that he would leave UConn to enter the [[2011 NBA Draft]] on April 12.<ref>{{cite web|last= |first= |title=Sources: Kemba Walker going pro |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=6331070 |work=ESPN.com |date=April 12, 2011 |accessdate=April 12, 2011}}</ref>

==Personal==
Walker grew up in the Sack-Wern Houses in [[Soundview, Bronx]], and is the youngest of three siblings.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/hschool/2007/06/19/2007-06-19_walk_this_way.html |title=Walk this way: Kemba can relax, now that he's settled on Connecticut |first=Ian |last=Begley |newspaper=[[New York Daily News]] |date=June 19, 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/2011/03/11/2011-03-11_kemba_walker_and_dwight_hardy_both_make_bronx_proud_at_garden_but_walker_steals_.html |title=Kemba Walker and Dwight Hardy both make Bronx proud at Garden, but Walker steals the spotlight |first=Mike |last=Lupica |authorlink=Mike Lupica |newspaper=New York Daily News |date=March 11, 2011 }}</ref> His mother is [[St. Croix|Crucian]] and his father is [[Antiguan]]. Walker is also a dancer. He performed three times at the [[Apollo Theater]] for the TV show [[Showtime at the Apollo]].<ref>{{cite news |title=UConn's Kemba Walker retraces steps to Manhattan's Rice High School |newspaper=New York Daily News |date=November 25, 2009 |first=Roger |last=Rubin |url=http://articles.nydailynews.com/2009-11-25/sports/17938869_1_apollo-theater-big-dance-troupe}}</ref>
